description: Nodegroup Behind the Cluster Kubernetes Version
rationale: The nodes carry the kubelet, the container runtime and the kernel that actually run the workloads, so a nodegroup left on an older Kubernetes version keeps running the AMI release built for that version and misses the fixes shipped since, including those for kubelet and container escape issues. A control plane upgrade does nothing for the nodes, and EKS only supports a limited version skew, so a nodegroup that stays behind eventually blocks the next control plane upgrade as well.
remediation: Update the nodegroup to the Kubernetes version of the cluster, which replaces its nodes with instances running the matching EKS optimized AMI release
